title: "Near or Distant? Elite Climate Rhetoric and Public Opinion in Ireland"
date: "2026"

  - name: "James P. Cross"

abstract: "Legislators can portray climate impacts as already affecting people close to home or as a threat to distant populations and future generations. Whether these portrayals change public opinion remains unclear. Previous experiments have yielded mixed findings, and differences in how they manipulate psychological distance, alongside limited power to detect small effects, make the evidence difficult to interpret. || Using a preregistered survey experiment with a nationally representative sample of adults in Ireland, we test whether near or distant portrayals shift climate policy support and behavioural intentions. A conjoint then examines what makes climate rhetoric persuasive: how messages describe who is affected and where, and how the speaker’s gender, nationality and political alignment shape those judgements. || Both stages pair text with AI-generated speech. In the conjoint, voices match the speaker’s stated gender and signal nationality through Irish or continental European accents. Respondents hear these cues as well as read them, allowing us to vary how the speaker sounds while holding the message constant."
